transport_notes: Requests are [operation, command ID, payload]. Responses/notifications are [status, command ID, payload]. All multi-byte integers are little-endian; signed integers use two's complement.
Read means writing a read request to the characteristic; the GATT characteristic exposes WRITE, INDICATE, NOTIFY, not GATT READ.

Legacy BLE: Subscribe to indications for command replies and notifications for updates. Serialize requests. ATT write completion is not protocol completion. Shifter writes finish via a later notification. Most successful writes echo the request payload; read back when setters can normalize or ignore values.

Canonical booleans are one byte, 0 or 1. Legacy firmware accepts nonzero true and often ignores trailing write bytes (the old app sends two boolean bytes). This library emits canonical packets and accepts legacy boolean write echoes only when requested explicitly.

Strings are unprefixed bytes with no on-wire terminator. New clients use UTF-8 and exclude embedded NUL because firmware string setters use C strings. Firmware does not validate UTF-8; C codecs expose byte views.
Errors begin FF <ID>; some legacy paths echo additional request bytes. Do not decode an error payload as a setting. Packets shorter than two bytes can be silently ignored by firmware.

Normal ATT value capacity is MTU-3. In legacy mode, snapshot chunks and scan events have explicit fragmentation; other large values (including 63-byte power rows, needing MTU >=66) require sufficient MTU or a transport-supported long write. Secure v1 uses its bounded record fragments at smaller MTUs.

Legacy DirCon carries the same custom protocol bytes: first command response in characteristic-write response, updates as notifications. Snapshot remaining chunks follow as notifications; current DirCon snapshot payload is 200 bytes per chunk.
Snapshot header: status@0, ID@1, version u8@2, chunk u16@3, count u16@5, JSON bytes@7. Count >0, chunk<count. Snapshot transfer blocks other BLE commands and expires after 5000 ms without progress.

Scan header: status@0, ID@1, version u8@2, event u8@3, scan ID u16@4, sequence u16@6, fragment u8@8, count u8@9, body@10. Count >0, fragment<count. Begin/end carry no body. Device body is [UUID length u8, UUID UTF-8, name UTF-8].
Manifest versions identify the library. The capabilities bit field selects the secure v1 handshake. Existing command IDs, characteristic UUIDs and legacy payload layouts are preserved.
App metadata contains presentation defaults/ranges from the companion app, not firmware-enforced limits or board-dependent factory defaults. Wire validity and application policy are separate.

With capability bit 1, only capabilities and secure v1 discovery/handshake frames are public. All settings, updates, logs and firmware operations travel inside authenticated secure records. See docs/secure.md for the handshake, replay rules and transport framing.

Inside a secure record, status 0x81 marks an unsolicited setting change, scan event or log. It never acknowledges a write or read. Request-bound snapshot chunks carry success 0x80. Shifter writes receive an explicit command acknowledgement.

commands.name: allSettings
commands.notes: Read-only user-config JSON snapshot, not every runtime measurement. Reassemble UTF-8 bytes before parsing JSON. Unknown JSON keys must be ignored. The password field is empty when the device supports password-write-only capability. Retry from the start after disconnect, missing chunks or inconsistent framing.

commands.name: scanResults
commands.notes: Notification-only scan stream. Trigger with 02 24. Begin sequence is zero; device sequences start at zero; end sequence is number of devices. Reassemble fragments per scan ID and sequence, then parse [UUID byte length, UUID UTF-8, name UTF-8]. End does not guarantee that all notifications arrived.

commands.name: gearTeeth
commands.notes: Pair = front*100+rear. Zero pairs selects Unlimited; otherwise 2-26 unique pairs, front/rear 1-99, rounded ratio 500-6000 thousandths. Firmware sorts by ratio then packed pair. Write selects preset 0. Named preset 1 makes tooth reads fail. Metadata/changed response is count only; indexed reads add index and pair. Save using 02 18. Maximum write is 55 bytes (ATT MTU >=58).

app.textDescription: Choose the gears your virtual shifter simulates in simulation (incline) mode. Unlimited moves the knob by Shift Step on every click, with no top or bottom gear. A groupset gives you a fixed set of gears, and each shift moves in proportion to the real ratio change between them. ERG mode is unaffected.

commands.name: gearPreset
commands.notes: 0 selects Unlimited (or identifies custom teeth on read); 1 selects Mixed Terrain 1x24. Unknown IDs fail. Read 0x34 as well to distinguish Unlimited from a bounded tooth profile. Save using 02 18.

app.textDescription: Built-in groupset ratio table. 0 uses the tooth pairs, or Unlimited when there are none.

commands.name: capabilities
commands.description: Public protocol capabilities. Version byte and LE32 bits. Bit 0 makes WiFi password write-only. Bit 1 requires secure settings and firmware streaming. Bit 2 permits 2048-byte DirCon OTA chunks. Bit 3 permits a four-chunk BLE OTA window when Write Without Response is available.

commands.name: firmwareStream
commands.description: Authenticated application image stream. Begin carries size LE32 and binary SHA256, chunk carries offset LE32 and bytes, finish and abort have no fields. Reply carries the operation and next offset LE32.
commands.notes: Authenticated application image stream. Begin carries size LE32 and binary SHA256, chunk carries offset LE32 and bytes, finish and abort have no fields. Reply carries the operation and next offset LE32. Capability bit 2 (0x04) permits the authenticated DirCon transfer owner to send up to 2048 image bytes in one unfragmented encrypted chunk after BEGIN succeeds. BLE, other commands and replies keep the existing record limits. Capability bit 3 (0x08) permits up to four single-value BLE OTA chunks in flight using Write Without Response, each with its own authenticated next-offset acknowledgement.
